what_it_does: This chip brings deep neural network inference—the computation performed when an AI model makes a prediction—directly into memory using a technology called MRAM (a type of magnetic storage that retains data without power). Instead of constantly fetching weights (the learned parameters of the model) from external storage to the processor, this chip embeds 1.1 megabits of weights inside the silicon itself, eliminating wasteful data movement. It combines analog matrix multiplication (using magnetic crossbar arrays as a primitive calculator for neural networks) with the on-chip weight storage, designed to run complete AI models on battery-powered sensor devices. The key innovation is that the entire system is monolithic—built as a single unified chip—rather than a collection of separate components.
